properties.statement:
THE CONDITION ANTHONY ATTACHED TO THE SE DEFERRAL HAS CLEARED, and nothing in reflow2 computes that.

His ruling of 2026-08-16 was 'DO IT, BUT NOT YET' — 'this is not immediate (priority is resolving bugs)' — and the sequencing was stated as part of the ruling rather than as a note beside it: '`epoch:instruments-stop-overstating` and its five requirements come before this.'

AS OF 2026-08-17 THAT EPOCH IS CLOSED. `arrival_delta` reports 5 of 5 delivered, `missed_obligations: []`, `movement: []`, and it shipped as v0.34.0 (`rel:v0340`, deployed; tag pushed; release verified to have published 5 assets). So the named blocker is gone.

WHAT THIS FACT IS FOR: it is not a request to start the SE work — that is the owner's call and 'the bug work is done' is not the same statement as 'do this next'. It exists because a DEFERRAL WITH A STATED PRECONDITION HAS NO WAY TO NOTICE THE PRECONDITION CLEARING. The decision is `accepted`, so it raises no gap; `loop_status` counts open decisions and this one is settled; `arrival_delta` reads schedules and this carries none. A deferral therefore goes quiet at exactly the moment it should speak. `cap:revise-trigger` (planned) is the general answer — trace new evidence back through GOVERNED_BY to the Decisions it bears on — and this is a concrete instance of what it would catch.

RELATED MEASUREMENTS ALREADY ON THE RECORD, unchanged by the deferral: 73 coupled module pairs with ZERO sharing a declared Interface, 51 of them crossing a subsystem boundary; all 15 Interfaces sit at the SYSTEM edge and none describes an internal boundary; and `fact:the-eight-subsystems-are-groupings-not-black-boxes` (2026-08-17) adds that 0 of 8 subsystems PROVIDE anything.
